name: udecimal-u256
instr:
I'm restoring the core operations in our copy of `udecimal` so callers can use its fixed-point decimals for financial calculations and format the results. The package still has methods that panic in `decimal.go`, `codec.go`, `bint.go`, and `u128.go`. Could you implement the missing decimal arithmetic, comparisons, rounding, powers and square roots, integer conversion, and fixed-precision string formatting, together with the underlying integer operations?

The doc comments on the missing operations are the contract; please follow them so existing callers get the documented behavior. Keep the existing public API names and signatures unchanged for compatibility. `QuoRem` truncates the quotient toward zero and bounds the remainder by absolute magnitude. `StringFixed` preserves significant fractional digits and removes fractional trailing zeros beyond the requested minimum. Unsigned 128-bit multiplication overflow and subtraction underflow return `errOverflow`. I'll run the package's own tests to check the restored operations, and the rest of the project's tests must keep passing.

In the non-test code you add, please avoid: new `init()` functions; the `syscall`, `golang.org/x/sys`, `os/exec`, `os/signal`, `plugin`, `embed`, `runtime/cgo`, `runtime/pprof`, `runtime/trace`, `testing` and `flag` packages, cgo, and `//go:linkname`, `//go:embed`, `//line` or `/*line` directives; `os.Exit`, `os.StartProcess`, `os.FindProcess` and `runtime.Goexit`; reading `os.Args`, `os.Executable`, `/
